Absorption, Transport, and Storage
Cholesterol absorption
Cholesterol in the intestinal lumen typically consists of one-third dietary cholesterol and two-thirds biliary cholesterol. The average
daily diet contains 300–500 mg of cholesterol obtained from animal products. The bile provides an additional 800–1200 mg of
cholesterol throughout each day as gallbladder contractions provide a ﬂow of bile acids, cholesterol, and phospholipids to facilitate
